about: Canary token registry for the fleet's copyable prompts (Andrew approved Oct 30, 2026). Each public copyable prompt carries ONE unique trailing token of the form [ref: AH-<slug>-<hash6>], where hash6 is the first 6 hex chars of SHA-256("AH-canary:" + slug). The token survives a plain-text copy, is inert when pasted into an AI chat, and does not change the prompt's meaning. Purpose: if a prompt resurfaces publicly (a page, a repo, a post), an exact-match search for its token proves the copy came from Andrew's distribution and identifies which prompt traveled. The Tuesday site-health watch (LEG F) reads THIS file as its search list and keeps its seen-list beside the watch's other state. Tokens are deliberately public — a canary only works if it is copied along, and knowing the format lets anyone strip it, so this detects honest republication, not determined laundering. Prompts are the unit: one token per prompt, shared by every surface that copies the same canonical text (e.g. the AIMF trial prompt is copied from both the AIMF page and the site card; both fetch the same canonical file, so both yield the same token).
